title: Sleep Matters: Profiling Sleep Patterns to Predict Sports Injuries in Recreational Runners
claims: The secondary analysis used survey data from 425 Dutch recreational runners, identifying sleep profiles from sleep duration, sleep quality, and sleep problems.
Runners in the Poor Sleepers profile were significantly more likely to report sports injuries than Steady Sleepers (OR 1.78, 95% CI 1.14-2.78; p=0.01), with a 68% injury probability.
The Efficient Sleepers and Fragmented Sleepers profiles did not differ significantly from the Steady Sleepers reference group.
All predictor variables together explained 5% of injury variance, and the cross-sectional design does not allow causal inference.
The paper treats sleep duration and quality together as an injury-risk factor and advises prioritising sleep as a recovery need, especially after returning from injury.
